title: A Wolf for the Sigil
premise: Sable Villalobos, a temple scribe bound by debt to the magicless valley of Corren Hollow, discovers her own face in a century-old book of prophecies — and is pulled through the sigil-ink into the kingdom of Vael, where King Aldric wears a crown that is slowly devouring him. To survive, she must ally with Wren, a wolf-shifter outcast sworn to the crown he despises, and unbind the king before the thing beneath the crown completes its hundred-year hunger. As Sable's debt-magic proves to be the one force that can rewrite prophecy, she and Wren fall in love across the fault line of their duties. In the end she chooses truth over loyalty to her temple, shatters the crown at the cost of her binding — freeing herself, the king, and Wren's pack — though the price leaves the valley's magicless peace broken forever.
about_author: Lena Whitlock is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery far older than themselves, from a farmhouse office guarded by an opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In Corren Hollow, Sable copies ledgers for the temple that owns her debt, counting the years until freedom. A strange new book arrives for cataloguing, its pages warm to the touch. Emotional beat: restless longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cataloguing late, she finds a prophecy dated a century past describing tonight — her name, her face, a wolf at her side. When she touches the page, the ink pulls her through. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into terror.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Under a Hungry Sky
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She lands in Vael mid-prophecy: a coronation procession, crowds chanting, and a king whose shadow moves wrong. Captured as a spy, she meets Wren, the wolf-shifter assigned to guard her cell. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Wolf Who Hates His Leash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren interrogates the stranger his oath says he must distrust, but her knowledge of the crown's secret rites unsettles him. He hides what he knows: the king is already half-consumed. Emotional beat: duty grinding against instinct.

chapters.title: What the Crown Whispers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Brought before King Aldric, Sable hears the crown speaking through him — offering her debt-freedom in exchange for completing the prophecy. She refuses, and something ancient marks her for it. Emotional beat: temptation met with fear-fueled resolve.

chapters.title: Old Debts, Older Magic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren breaks Sable out, not from kindness but because the crown wants her used. They flee into the Thornwood, where his pack once lived before the crown exiled them. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, first flicker of trust.

chapters.title: The Pack That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the ruined den, Sable learns Wren's history: he swore loyalty to the crown to spare his pack, and they died anyway. She shows him the prophecy book; his death is written on its final pages. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown sends hollowed knights after them. A brutal running fight through the Thornwood forces Sable to use her scribe's craft — rewriting a ward-sigil mid-battle — proving her magic works here. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into capability.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sheltering with a heretic archivist, Sable learns the truth: her valley exists because the last scribe sealed all magic there, and her debt-bound contract was designed to breed a successor. She was never free. Emotional beat: betrayal by everything she served.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Chains
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren offers to take her back to Corren Hollow, away from prophecy. Sable realizes leaving means Aldric dies and the crown goes hunting. Their argument cracks open into a near-confession of feeling neither can afford. Emotional beat: love acknowledged, then deferred.

chapters.title: The Court of Ashes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They infiltrate the capital during the Feast of Binding, disguised among pilgrim scribes. Sable witnesses the crown feeding on courtiers' memories to stay anchored. Emotional beat: horror laced with grim clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: A Dance with the Devoured
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the feast, Wren dances with the queen-regent, who is not what she seems — she's the crown's first victim, wearing a stolen body, begging him in fragments to end it. Emotional beat: pity entangled with revulsion.

chapters.title: The Page That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The prophecy book surfaces in the royal archive; reading ahead, Sable sees Wren die protecting her and a version of herself crowned instead. She tears the page — and the world flinches. Emotional beat: hubris and heartbreak intertwined.

chapters.title: Torn Pages Have Teeth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tearing the page destabilizes the prophecy: reality begins improvising, violently. The crown's hunters find them because the book now screams their location. Wren chooses to stand and fight rather than run again. Emotional beat: fatalism burned away by commitment.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Breaks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered, Sable is offered a bargain by the temple's envoy: return home, debt erased, prophecy fulfilled without her. Accepting means abandoning Wren and Aldric. She refuses aloud, breaking her contract's hold. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — truth over loyalty.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach Aldric, buried alive inside his own mind by the crown. Wren, sworn to the crown, must break his oath word by word while Sable anchors the king's fading self with stories of his true reign. Emotional beat: sacrifice as devotion.

chapters.title: Sigil and Fang
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crown, starving, takes the queen-regent's body and hunts them through the burning palace. Sable fights it with rewritten sigils while Wren holds the line in wolf-form, prophecy pages scattering like embers. Emotional beat: desperate, blazing momentum toward climax.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Climax. On the coronation dais, Sable uses her debt-contract itself as ink, writing the crown's unbinding in her own binding — paying her debt with her freedom. The crown shatters; Aldric wakes; the seal on Corren Hollow cracks. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Hundred Years
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The kingdom reels; Aldric, freed but diminished, pardons the shifters and names Wren his truth-speaker. Wren searches the ashes for Sable and finds only the prophecy book, its final page now blank. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by absence.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot It Was Safe
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable wakes in Corren Hollow, expelled by her own unbinding, as magic seeps back into the valley she thought eternal. Her temple masters are powerless now; she is not. Emotional beat: home no longer fitting, and no longer needing to.

chapters.title: Written in the Margins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, Sable finds new text appearing in the old prophecy book — Wren's handwriting, carried across the seal by the bond their story wrote. He is coming; the book is how. Emotional beat: hope arriving sideways, earned.

chapters.title: A Wolf at the Door
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Wren crosses into the changed valley at dawn, oath-free for the first time in his life. Sable meets him not as scribe or debtor or prophesied instrument, but simply as herself. They begin a story no book has written yet. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not owed.
